question: Under recorded remote viewing conditions, do independent observers show a directional temporal-stability preference between a six-second Q8 sequence and NATURAL32, with Q4 retained as a diagnostic cost point?

standardsBasis.scope: remote controlled-record study informed by BT.500; not represented as a calibrated BT.500 laboratory implementation

b26GapAudit.sourceMismatch: B26 compares three B25 NATURAL32 replicate sequences; it does not compare NATURAL32, Q4 and Q8.
b26GapAudit.distributionGap: B26 observer sessions remain local ignored work and have not been distributed to independent observers.
b26GapAudit.responseGap: B26 downloads response JSON but has no accepted-response validator, locked response ledger or unblinded formal analyzer.
b26GapAudit.reuseDecision: reuse the proven lossless carrier and blinding patterns, but create new B34 sources, mappings, sessions and response tooling

renderDesign.realizationScope: one frozen six-second realization per method; no whole-sequence cross-process repeatability claim

displayTransform.method: write scene-linear composites, load them in frozen Blender/OCIO, and save_render through the pinned scene display/view settings

carrier.acceptance: decode all 144 frames to RGB and require 144/144 exact display-PNG pixels, maximum error 0 and zero changed RGB pixels

resourceGate.componentExrRetention: retain until package result and all hashes are committed; later cleanup requires an explicit recorded action and remains reproducible by rerun

observerDesign.balanceAtTarget: each method-order permutation appears exactly three times

blinding.mappingCommitment: SHA-256 over canonical session mapping plus independent 32-byte salt
blinding.mappingStorage: sealed ignored local work; absent from observer package and public manifest
blinding.unblindRule: a response must be hash-locked before that session is analyzed; unused session mappings remain sealed

responseChain.observerOutput: one immutable JSON response download with canonical SHA-256
responseChain.validator: bind response to spec, session commitment, carrier hashes, complete fields, playback telemetry and response hash
responseChain.acceptedLedger: append accepted anonymous response hashes; never overwrite an accepted response
responseChain.formalAnalyzer: may emit a formal outcome only when 18 valid independent responses form the frozen balanced schedule
responseChain.privacy: do not collect names, email addresses or raw vision-health details

formalDecision.q8PreferenceSupport: At least 14 of all 18 valid observers directionally choose Q8 as more stable than NATURAL32, and the count rating Q8 MILD-or-worse is not greater than the NATURAL32 count.
formalDecision.naturalPreferenceSupport: At least 14 of all 18 valid observers directionally choose NATURAL32 as more stable than Q8, and the count rating NATURAL32 MILD-or-worse is not greater than the Q8 count.
formalDecision.noDirectionalDifference: At least 14 of all 18 choose INDISTINGUISHABLE for Q8 versus NATURAL32 and no more than two observers rate either primary method MILD-or-worse.
formalDecision.q4Rule: Q4 single-clip and pairwise observations are secondary descriptive results and cannot change the primary Q8-versus-NATURAL decision.

nonClaims: Package generation, carrier integrity and interface automation are not human observations.
The remote study is informed by ITU-R BT.500-15 but is not a calibrated BT.500 laboratory implementation.
One six-second realization does not establish whole-sequence or cross-machine render repeatability.
Motion blur is disabled; the study does not validate motion-blur quality.
A Q8 preference or no-difference result would apply only to these carriers, observers and recorded viewing conditions.
Temporal-stability preference is not a judgment of acting, narrative, composition or general cinematic merit.
The study does not validate 4K projection, another scene, another engine, a delivery codec or the optimality of the Q8 point set.
